conventions.convention: Projected subgradients support the finite-valued convex objective over its feasible domain C. The observed best iterate and weighted average use x_0 through x_{N-1}, excluding the final updated point x_N; weights are positive stepsizes.

Poll lists are finite, nonempty, ordered and positive spanning in dimension n≥1. Directions need not be normalized; the directional score uses minus the inner product, and the estimates retain the largest direction norm.

Direct search accepts the first in-domain trial with strict decrease f(y)<f(x_k)−ρ(Δ_k), skips out-of-domain trials without evaluation, and counts polls separately from objective calls. Its forcing ratio tends to zero as the mesh tends to zero.

The bundle stores every successful oracle cut. Predicted decrease is F(x_k)−M_k(z_k), without subtracting the quadratic term; equality in the serious-step acceptance test accepts. Null steps retain the center and append the trial cut.

Bundle convergence concerns an infinite exact continuation with fixed positive stabilizer, continuous finite restriction to a closed convex effective domain, compact initial sublevel set, touching underestimating models, positive predicted decreases and vanishing aggregate-model errors. Full memory alone does not establish the error premise.

Nelder–Mead sorts objective ties by current vertex slot and retains the earliest evaluated best point on ties. Inside contraction requires strict improvement; outside contraction accepts equality. Shrink makes fresh calls and commits only a complete valid update. Tolerance-met requires both diameter and spread tolerances.
The fixed-step square-root schedule requires R>0 and G>0. When either bound is zero, the stated boundary conclusion concerns the best-iterate gap and does not prescribe a zero stepsize.

load_bearing.statement: Under the projected-subgradient update, for x*∈C and a successful kth call returning g_k∈∂f(x_k), ‖x_{k+1}−x*‖²≤‖x_k−x*‖²−2α_k(f(x_k)−f(x*))+α_k²‖g_k‖².
For nonempty closed convex C⊆R^n, t>0, v∈R^n and a nonempty finite list of affine functions m_i, max_i m_i(y)+‖y−v‖²/(2t) has a unique global minimizer on C.
For every finite positive-spanning list D in R^n, n≥1, its directional score on the unit sphere attains a strictly positive minimum κ_D. Thus every v∈R^n admits a direction d_i with −〈v,d_i〉≥κ_D‖v‖.
For an open U⊆R^n and an everywhere totally differentiable f:U→R with L-Lipschitz gradient, L≥0, if x,y∈U and [x,y]⊆U, then f(y)≤f(x)+〈∇f(x),y−x〉+(L/2)‖y−x‖².

For proper closed convex F with nonempty closed convex domain C, fixed t>0, x∈C, a finite affine model M≤F on C, its exact quadratically regularized minimizer z over C, error e=F(z)−M(z), and p=prox_{tF}(x), one has ‖z−p‖²≤4te.
If F:R^n→(−∞,+∞] is convex, t>0, and p minimizes Q(y)=F(y)+‖y−v‖²/(2t) with finite Q(p), then Q(z)≥Q(p)+‖z−p‖²/(4t) for every finite-valued F(z).
For compact K⊆R^n contained in open V, there is δ>0 such that x∈K and ‖y−x‖<δ imply y∈V. If K is empty, any positive δ works.

For a successful N-step projected-subgradient run on nonempty closed convex C with convex f, positive stepsizes, a global minimizer x*, ‖g_k‖≤G and R≥‖x_0−x*‖, both the minimum observed objective gap and the stepsize-weighted-average gap are at most (R²+G²Σ_{k<N}α_k²)/(2Σ_{k<N}α_k).

alerts.finding: In thm-nearest-point-in-a-nonempty-closed-convex-set, Proof 1.1 says: “Choose $c_0\in C$ and put $R=\|x-c_0\|_2$. The set $K=C\cap\overline B(x,R)$ is nonempty, closed, and bounded”. The allowed case x=c_0 gives R=0, whereas def-metric-ball explicitly states: “The radius is always a strictly positive real; a ball of radius $0$ or of negative radius is never written in this library.” Thus the proof uses undefined ball notation at an admissible boundary, including C={x}. The nearest-point claim itself remains true.
